summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and a known aortic arch thrombus was admitted for recurrent pleuritic chest pain, now on the right side, and chronic abdominal pain. Imaging, including a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, showed no new pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, or abdominal pathology. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, likely exacerbated by chronic cough and prior respiratory issues. Abdominal pain was attributed to prior surgeries and Lovenox injection site discomfort. The elevated white blood cell count was due to recent steroid use, not infection. The patient expressed ongoing struggles with chronic pain and anxiety, and though he declined narcotics refill, follow-up was arranged with primary care for comprehensive pain and mental health management. He remained on anticoagulation with Lovenox and was discharged home in stable condition.
